sentences.text: Researchers investigated whether a chronic parasitic brain infection protects mice from lethal malaria, linking this protection to a specific pattern of gene activity that increased TGF-beta and the IL-33/ST2 signaling pair.

Analysis of brain cells revealed that the chronic parasite altered astrocytes into a mixed type displaying both inflammatory and calming markers, which became a main source of IL-33 proteins and attracted specific immune cells called ILC2s.
The authors suggest that because mice lacking the gene for IL-33 still showed some protection, the protective mechanism may not be entirely dependent on this specific molecule.
